declared_purpose: Interactive programming tutoring through lessons, code review, debugging, algorithms, projects, design patterns, interviews and language learning. Progress persistence is explicitly required; analysis and test scripts are optional enhancements (SKILL.md:3-5, 648-697, 722-729).

data_operations.data_scope: Programming experience, learning goals, preferred teaching style, editor setup, ability to run code and git familiarity.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tutor conversation; hosting and transport boundaries are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: During initial assessment; the entry document also permits starting directly with a request.

data_operations.data_scope: Submitted code or referenced files; errors and exact inputs/outputs; project requirements, intended users and constraints; interview reasoning.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tutor conversation and applicable analysis tools; no separate external recipient is specified.
data_operations.condition: According to the selected review, debugging, project or interview mode.

data_operations.operation: Infer learning attributes and adapt instruction
data_operations.source: Learner responses, comprehension and demonstrated performance
data_operations.data_scope: Mastery, practice needs, solved problems, current concepts and suitable difficulty or pacing.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tutor's working context; selected attributes are also designated for the learning log.
data_operations.condition: During adaptive teaching and progress assessment.

data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tutor context and explanations returned to the learner.
data_operations.condition: When the learner asks about a relevant topic; the listed examples are reference material, not automatic execution paths.

data_operations.data_scope: Dated session history, covered topics, solved problems and difficulty, practiced modes/languages, insights and challenges, dated mastery, review reasons and goal status.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: references/user-progress/learning_log.md through the agent's Edit tool.
data_operations.condition: Explicitly mandatory after sessions, significant milestones, save requests and quiz/interview practice. The packaged file currently contains an empty template.

data_operations.operation: Read and statically analyze a selected source file
data_operations.data_scope: Entire file, including comments and literals; Python AST or JavaScript checks produce issues and code metrics. Password detection produces a finding label rather than reproducing the matched value.
data_operations.condition: Only when the optional analyzer is invoked; implemented analysis supports Python and JavaScript-family extensions. This path parses or scans source without executing it.

data_operations.operation: Read source and estimate function complexity
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied Python filepath or code argument
data_operations.data_scope: Entire module or supplied snippet; function names, line numbers, recursion, operations and complexity estimates. The --function filter applies after the whole file is read and parsed.
data_operations.condition: Only when the optional file or snippet analysis path is invoked; source is parsed rather than executed.

data_operations.operation: Return static-analysis results to the caller
data_operations.data_scope: Code analyzer: filepath, language, metrics, issue locations/messages and suggestions. Complexity analyzer: function identifiers, locations, estimates and suggestions. Error paths print diagnostic information.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output or standard error, normally returned to the invoking caller; no additional transmission or report file is implemented.
data_operations.condition: When an analyzer runs; text or JSON depends on the requested format.

data_operations.operation: Inspect a local test target to select a framework
data_operations.source: Test target and current working directory
data_operations.data_scope: Entire Python test file for marker matching; target type/extensions and existence of pytest.ini or setup.cfg. Configuration contents are not read by this detector.
data_operations.condition: Only when --framework is omitted; directory detection uses configuration existence checks.

data_operations.operation: Delegate test execution to a subprocess
data_operations.source: Selected test target and ambient process context
data_operations.data_scope: Target argument and inherited execution environment; executed tests, imports and framework configuration determine further access.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local python -m pytest, python -m unittest discover, or npx jest child process.
data_operations.condition: Only when the optional test runner is invoked. Each subprocess has a 60-second timeout; no explicit environment or working-directory override is supplied. Additional reads, network activity, persistence and deletion remain unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Capture test output and return parsed summaries
data_operations.source: Test subprocess standard output and standard error
data_operations.data_scope: Complete captured streams are concatenated and split in memory. Returned results contain counts, available duration and, for pytest/unittest failures, test identifiers with a generic message; the wrapper also prints the framework and target.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Raw streams: local run_tests.py memory. Parsed results: standard output to its caller. No explicit raw-output persistence or secure deletion is implemented.
data_operations.condition: For all three test frameworks; actual output content depends on tests and external framework behavior.

data_operations.data_scope: Dependency names and version constraints supplied to pip, or the Jest package request supplied to npm.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local pip/npm processes if the documented commands are followed; external endpoints and installation storage are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Manual optional setup, not automatic skill execution. Package-manager network and persistence behavior is outside the supplied implementation.

potential_excess.data_scope: Raw test stdout/stderr beyond the status lines, identifiers and timing fields used by the wrapper, including any diagnostic or application output present.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Test subprocess pipes into run_tests.py memory, with additional concatenated and split representations.
potential_excess.condition: Whenever tests emit output beyond the parsed summary fields; pytest explicitly requests short tracebacks.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The optional runner's purpose is test execution with formatted feedback. Complete diagnostic capture is an implementation choice; most captured content is neither parsed nor returned.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Execute the selected tests and preserve accurate supported counts, failure identifiers and timing.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Suppress unused traceback bodies and consume bounded status/summary output, or use a structured result channel. This narrows data within the required execution action rather than removing test execution.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Maintain the current result fields and reliable failure detection; retain additional diagnostics only when needed for requested debugging feedback.

potential_excess.data_scope: Accumulating session-level narratives about insights, breakthroughs and challenges, alongside dated learning activity and current mastery/review/goals.
potential_excess.condition: As instructed session entries accumulate; the supplied template contains no actual learner history.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Progress persistence and session history are explicit requirements. Open-ended narrative detail and its continuing verbosity can exceed what is needed for instructional continuity.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Save progress at the required triggers, maintain the specified progress categories and session history, and confirm the save.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use compact topic/problem tags and brief pedagogical notes; summarize older narrative detail while retaining required session entries and useful current learning state.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve dates, relevant accomplishments, review reasons, goal status and information needed to resume teaching. Do not remove mandatory progress persistence.
